We need to produce a test class for AnyOfValidator.walk method. Need to initialize fields and dependencies. We need to test behavior: when shouldValidateSchema true -> it should call validate and return its result. When false -> it should iterate schemas and call walk on each, and return empty set.

We can mock dependencies: ExecutionContext, JsonNode, JsonNodePath, etc. Also need an instance of AnyOfValidator. Its constructor requires SchemaLocation, JsonNodePath evaluationPath, JsonNode schemaNode (which must be array), JsonSchema parentSchema, ValidationContext validationContext.

We can create a simple schemaNode as an ArrayNode with two entries, each being an empty object node, using Jackson's ObjectMapper. We'll need a ValidationContext: we can mock it or create real one using JsonMetaSchema and JsonSchemaFactory. Simpler: mock ValidationContext and stub newSchema to return mock JsonSchema objects.

But AnyOfValidator's constructor loops over schemaNode array and calls validationContext.newSchema(...). So we need to stub that method. ValidationContext class has method newSchema? Not shown but likely exists. We'll mock ValidationContext and stub newSchema to return mock JsonSchema.

Thus we can create mock ValidationContext, mock JsonSchema parent (maybe null). Use a dummy SchemaLocation (new SchemaLocation(new AbsoluteIri("http://example.com"), new JsonNodePath(JsonNodePath.PathType.JSON_POINTER))) but AbsoluteIri class not described. Simpler: we can mock SchemaLocation as well.

But constructor expects actual SchemaLocation object; we can mock it (using Mockito) as it's just stored. Provide mock.

Also JsonNodePath evaluationPath can be mock.

Create schemaNode as ArrayNode with two empty object nodes using JsonNodeFactory.instance.arrayNode().add(JsonNodeFactory.instance.objectNode())...

Now instantiate AnyOfValidator with these mocks.

Test 1: when shouldValidateSchema true, we need to stub validator's validate method? Actually walk will call validate(executionContext, node, rootNode, instanceLocation, true). That's a protected method in AnyOfValidator. We cannot easily stub it unless we spy the AnyOfValidator. Use Mockito.spy to spy the instance and stub the protected method using doReturn(...). But we can also test that result equals whatever we stub.

We'll use spy and doReturn(set).when(spy).validate(any(), any(), any(), any(), eq(true));

Then call walk with shouldValidateSchema true and assert returned set equals stub.

Test 2: when shouldValidateSchema false, we need to ensure each schema's walk is called. We'll create two mock JsonSchema objects, each with walk method returning something (maybe null). We'll verify that walk called with correct parameters. Also ensure that result is empty set.

Implementation details: need imports for Jackson, Set, LinkedHashSet, etc.

We'll also need to handle protected method canShortCircuit? Not needed.

Write test class with @BeforeEach to set up common objects: mock ExecutionContext, JsonNode node, rootNode, JsonNodePath instanceLocation, mock ValidationContext, mock SchemaLocation, mock JsonSchema parent (null). Create schemaNode array with two empty objects. Stub validationContext.newSchema to return mock JsonSchema objects (schema1, schema2). Then create AnyOfValidator instance.

In test for false: call walk(false) and verify schema1.walk called, schema2.walk called, and result empty.

In test for true: spy validator, stub validate to return a set with a dummy ValidationMessage (we can mock ValidationMessage). Return that set, call walk(true) and assert same.

Need to import ValidationMessage.
